domain_notes: The invariant interval of the closed geodesic through p and g^n(p) is exactly 2 (cosh(n b) - 1)(t^2 - x^2) + n^2 alpha^2. The winding-n loop is null on the POLARISED HYPERSURFACE x^2 - t^2 = n^2 alpha^2 / (2 (cosh(n b) - 1)) and timelike outside it. Because that radius decreases monotonically to zero as n grows, the union over all n is the whole region x^2 > t^2: alpha > 0 does NOT move the chronology horizon, which stays at x^2 = t^2 exactly as in Misner space. What alpha creates is the discrete family of polarised hypersurfaces that accumulates on the horizon, and those are where the renormalised stress tensor of a quantum field is singular. CTC-FA v2.0 locates them automatically from the deck group; see quotient_ctc.polarized_hypersurfaces.
